title: Chicken Jalfrezi
subtitle: Stir-fried chicken with peppers, tomato, and green chilli
excerpt: Chicken thighs cooked with green pepper, red onion, tomatoes, and plenty of green chilli in a dry-ish sauce that keeps the vegetables with a little bite. One of the few British-Indian curry house dishes with Chinese stir-fry roots.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jalfrezi is believed to have originated in colonial Bengal as a way to use up leftover roast meat, stir-frying it with onion, tomato, and green chilli. The technique has echoes of the Chinese-influenced cooking of Calcutta. By the 1990s it had become one of the most popular dishes in British Indian restaurants, known for its hot, relatively dry sauce and the presence of pepper strips.

recipeTools.notes: Wide pan or wok for stir-frying.

content.text: Jalfrezi works best at high heat, it is a stir-fry dish, not a slow braise. The vegetables should retain some texture; the sauce should coat rather than flood. Green chilli gives the heat. If you want it milder, deseed the chillies; if you want it hotter, add more. The dish comes together in under 30 minutes, which makes it one of the more practical weeknight curries.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless, cut into 3 cm pieces

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds. Add the chicken and cook without stirring for 2 minutes, then stir and cook for 3 more minutes until sealed. Remove and set aside.

In the same pan, add a little more oil if needed. Cook the onion over high heat for 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Add the garlic, ginger, and green chilli and cook for 2 minutes. Add the ground spices and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and 100 ml water. Cook for 10 minutes until the sauce reduces.

Return the chicken and add the pepper strips. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers are just tender. Stir in the garam masala and taste for salt. Scatter with coriander and serve with rice.
